title: AI phases at a glance: events, markets, usage and compute
summary: The AI evolution table by decade, the phases table on market size, usage, availability and compute, and the four key highlights.

chunks.heading: The AI evolution table
chunks.explanation_md:
The deck summarises the whole history in one table. Learn it row by row:

| Decade | Phase | Key events & milestones |
|---|---|---|
| 1950s to 1960s | Birth of AI | Turing Test proposed (1950); Dartmouth Conference (1956); early ML programs |
| 1970s | Early Hopes & Limitations | Rule-based systems; start of the first AI Winter due to unmet expectations |
| 1980s | Expert Systems Era | Rise of expert systems; knowledge engineering gains traction |
| 1990s | AI Rebounds | Deep Blue beats Kasparov (1997); progress in NLP and speech recognition |
| 2000s | ML Matures | Rise of algorithms like SVMs and decision trees; deep learning coined (2006) |
| 2010s | Deep Learning Revolution | AlexNet (2012) revolutionizes image recognition; GANs (2014), AlphaGo (2016) |
| 2020s | Foundation & Generative AI | LLMs like GPT-3, ChatGPT, DALL·E, Codex; AI regulations & IndiaAI Mission (2024) |
chunks.exam_line: Seven phases: Birth of AI, Early Hopes & Limitations, Expert Systems Era, AI Rebounds, ML Matures, Deep Learning Revolution, Foundation & Generative AI.

chunks.heading: Phases by market size and usage
chunks.explanation_md:
A second table looks at each phase through a business lens. First, **market size** and **primary usage**:

| Phase | Period | Market size & growth | Primary usage |
|---|---|---|---|
| Birth of AI | 1950s to 1960s | Mostly academic, minimal commercial investment | Symbolic AI, Turing Test, early chatbots (ELIZA) |
| Rule-based / Expert Systems | 1970s to 1980s | Grew into a **billion-dollar expert systems industry** by late 1980s | Industrial/domestic rule-based systems, diagnostics, ELIZA/PROLOG |
| AI Winter & ML Emergence | 1990s | Funding dropped; AI pivots to ML; **~$8 billion industry** by mid-2000s | Data mining, logistics, industrial automation, speech/NLP |
| ML & Deep Learning Rise | 2000s to 2010s | AI market **~$279 b in 2024**, projected **$1.8 t by 2030**; DL market **$125 b in 2025** | Web personalization, search engines, speech, image recognition |
| Deep Learning & Generative AI | 2010s to 2020s | DL market **~93 b (2024) to ~$1.42 t (2034)**, **CAGR ~31 to 35%** | ImageNet, GANs, AlphaGo (2016), ChatGPT, DALL·E |
chunks.exam_line: Market: about $8 billion by mid-2000s; AI market ~$279 b in 2024, projected $1.8 t by 2030; DL market ~93 b (2024) to ~$1.42 t (2034).

chunks.heading: Phases by availability and compute
chunks.explanation_md:
Now the same phases by **who could access AI** and **what powered it**:

| Phase | Availability / access | Compute power & data |
|---|---|---|
| Birth of AI | Limited to research labs/universities | Basic mainframes; extremely low compute & data capacity |
| Rule-based / Expert Systems | Business adoption by large firms; Lisp machines, specialized hardware | Modest compute; knowledge-engineering intensive |
| AI Winter & ML Emergence | Hidden in software back-ends; no "AI" label | Emergence of commodity PCs; larger datasets |
| ML & Deep Learning Rise | SaaS, cloud, APIs via AWS, Google, Microsoft | GPUs, clusters, big data; 2012 breakthrough (AlexNet) |
| Deep Learning & Generative AI | LLMs released to public, APIs, consumer apps; **democratized AI** | Massive transformer models; hyperscaler infrastructure investments |

Read down the access column and you see AI moving from research labs, to large firms, to hidden back-ends, to cloud APIs, to the public.
chunks.exam_line: Access went from research labs, to large firms, to hidden back-ends, to cloud APIs, to public LLMs; compute went from basic mainframes to GPUs and big data to massive transformer models.

chunks.heading: Key highlights: four shifts
chunks.explanation_md:
The deck's **key highlights** compress the table into four shifts:
1. **Markets are skyrocketing**: the total AI market exceeded **$279 b in 2024**, and DL alone is poised for **$1+ trillion by 2034**.
2. **Usage shifted** from academic/government labs to industrial applications, then to widespread commercial use, ending in **consumer-grade tools and enterprise-level deployments**.
3. **Availability evolved** from exclusive mainframes and specialized hardware to **accessible cloud services (AWS, Azure, etc.)** and later to **freely available APIs and consumer software**.
4. **Compute & data advanced** from basic mainframes to **powerful GPU clusters**; today's architectures, like **transformers**, demand immense computational resources from **hyperscalers**.
chunks.exam_line: Four shifts: markets skyrocketing ($279 b in 2024), usage from labs to consumers, availability from mainframes to cloud and APIs, compute from mainframes to GPU clusters.

questions.stem: State the four key highlights the slides draw from the AI phases table.
questions.model_answer_md:
The key highlights compress the whole phases table into **four shifts**.

1. **Markets are skyrocketing:** total AI market exceeded **$279 b in 2024**; DL alone is poised for **$1+ trillion by 2034**.
2. **Usage shifted:** from academic and government labs, to industrial applications, to widespread commercial use, ending in **consumer-grade tools and enterprise deployments**.
3. **Availability evolved:** from exclusive mainframes and specialized hardware, to **cloud services (AWS, Azure)**, to **freely available APIs and consumer software**.
4. **Compute and data advanced:** from basic mainframes to **powerful GPU clusters**; today's **transformers** need immense resources from **hyperscalers**.

AI grew bigger, more used, more open and more compute-hungry.

rubric.point: Markets: AI market over $279 b in 2024; DL poised for $1+ trillion by 2034
Usage: labs to industry to commercial to consumer and enterprise tools
Availability: mainframes to cloud (AWS, Azure) to free APIs and consumer software
Compute: mainframes to GPU clusters; transformers need hyperscalers

questions.stem: Using the phases table, how many times larger is the projected 2030 AI market than the 2024 AI market, and how many times larger is the 2034 DL market than in 2024?
questions.model_answer_md:
The **ML & Deep Learning Rise** and **Deep Learning & Generative AI** rows give the figures.

**AI market**
- 2024: about **$279 b**; 2030 projection: **$1.8 t** = 1,800 b.
- 1,800 / 279 = **6.45**, so the 2030 market is about **6.45 times** the 2024 market.

**Deep learning market**
- 2024: about **93 b**; 2034: about **$1.42 t** = 1,420 b.
- 1,420 / 93 = **15.27**, so about **15.27 times** larger, in line with a **CAGR of about 31 to 35%**.

DL is growing much faster than the AI market as a whole.

rubric.point: 1,800 / 279 = about 6.45 times
1,420 / 93 = about 15.27 times, consistent with CAGR ~31 to 35%

questions.stem: How did the availability of AI change across the phases, according to the slides?
questions.model_answer_md:
The **availability / access** column of the phases table shows AI moving steadily towards the public.

- **Birth of AI:** limited to **research labs and universities**.
- **Rule-based / Expert Systems:** **business adoption by large firms**; **Lisp machines** and specialized hardware.
- **AI Winter & ML Emergence:** **hidden in software back-ends**; no AI label.
- **ML & Deep Learning Rise:** **SaaS, cloud and APIs** via AWS, Google, Microsoft.
- **Deep Learning & Generative AI:** LLMs released to the public, APIs, consumer apps: **democratized AI**.

The key highlights call this a move from exclusive mainframes to freely available APIs and consumer software.

rubric.point: Birth of AI: limited to research labs and universities
Expert systems: large firms, Lisp machines, specialized hardware
1990s: hidden in software back-ends with no AI label
SaaS, cloud and APIs, then public LLMs and consumer apps: democratized AI

questions.stem: Explain the phases of AI through the four business lenses in the slides: market size, primary usage, availability and compute power.
questions.model_answer_md:
The deck reviews AI's history through a **business lens**: how big the market was, what AI was used for, who could access it and what powered it.

**1. Birth of AI (1950s to 1960s)**
- **Market:** mostly academic, minimal commercial investment.
- **Usage:** symbolic AI, Turing Test, early chatbots (**ELIZA**).
- **Access:** research labs and universities. **Compute:** basic mainframes, extremely low capacity.

**2. Rule-based / Expert Systems (1970s to 1980s)**
- **Market:** a **billion-dollar expert systems industry** by the late 1980s.
- **Usage:** rule-based systems, diagnostics, ELIZA/PROLOG.
- **Access:** large firms; **Lisp machines**. **Compute:** modest; knowledge-engineering intensive.

**3. AI Winter & ML Emergence (1990s)**
- **Market:** funding dropped, AI pivoted to ML, about **$8 billion industry** by the mid-2000s.
- **Usage:** data mining, logistics, industrial automation, speech/NLP.
- **Access:** hidden in software back-ends. **Compute:** commodity PCs, larger datasets.

**4. ML & Deep Learning Rise (2000s to 2010s)**
- **Market:** AI about **$279 b in 2024**, projected **$1.8 t by 2030**; DL **$125 b in 2025**.
- **Usage:** web personalization, search, speech, image recognition.
- **Access:** SaaS, cloud, APIs via **AWS, Google, Microsoft**. **Compute:** GPUs, clusters, big data; **AlexNet (2012)**.

**5. Deep Learning & Generative AI (2010s to 2020s)**
- **Market:** DL about **93 b (2024) to $1.42 t (2034)**, CAGR about **31 to 35%**.
- **Usage:** ImageNet, GANs, AlphaGo (2016), ChatGPT, DALL·E.
- **Access:** public LLMs and consumer apps: **democratized AI**. **Compute:** massive **transformer** models, **hyperscaler** investment.

**Key highlights:** markets are skyrocketing; usage moved from labs to consumer and enterprise tools; access moved from mainframes to cloud and free APIs; compute moved from mainframes to GPU clusters.

**Conclusion:** each phase made AI bigger, more widely used, easier to access and more compute-hungry.

rubric.point: Birth of AI: academic, symbolic AI and ELIZA, research labs, basic mainframes
Expert systems: billion-dollar industry by late 1980s, large firms, Lisp machines
1990s: ~$8 billion industry by mid-2000s; hidden in back-ends; commodity PCs
ML and DL rise: ~$279 b (2024), $1.8 t by 2030; cloud APIs; GPUs and AlexNet
Generative AI: DL ~93 b to ~$1.42 t, CAGR ~31 to 35%; democratized AI; transformers and hyperscalers
Key highlights: four shifts in market, usage, availability, compute

questions.stem: Describe the AI evolution table decade by decade, from the 1950s to the 2020s.
questions.model_answer_md:
The deck sums up AI's whole history in **one table** of decades, phases and milestones.

| Decade | Phase | Key events and milestones |
|---|---|---|
| 1950s to 1960s | **Birth of AI** | **Turing Test proposed (1950)**; **Dartmouth Conference (1956)**; early ML programs |
| 1970s | **Early Hopes & Limitations** | Rule-based systems; **start of the first AI Winter** due to unmet expectations |
| 1980s | **Expert Systems Era** | Rise of expert systems; **knowledge engineering** gains traction |
| 1990s | **AI Rebounds** | **Deep Blue beats Kasparov (1997)**; progress in NLP and speech recognition |
| 2000s | **ML Matures** | Algorithms like **SVMs and decision trees**; **deep learning coined (2006)** |
| 2010s | **Deep Learning Revolution** | **AlexNet (2012)** revolutionizes image recognition; **GANs (2014)**, **AlphaGo (2016)** |
| 2020s | **Foundation & Generative AI** | LLMs like **GPT-3, ChatGPT, DALL·E, Codex**; AI regulations and **IndiaAI Mission (2024)** |

**Reading the table as a story**
- **Rise:** the 1950s gave AI a test (Turing) and a name (Dartmouth).
- **Fall:** the 1970s brought the first AI Winter as rule-based systems fell short.
- **Business bet:** the 1980s turned to expert systems and knowledge engineering.
- **Return:** the 1990s showed real results (Deep Blue), the 2000s matured ML.
- **Boom:** the 2010s made deep learning dominant, and the 2020s brought generative AI and regulation, including India's own mission.

**Conclusion:** the table shows AI moving from a 1950 idea to 2020s foundation models, with a winter in between and a steady climb after it.

rubric.point: 1950s to 1960s Birth of AI: Turing Test (1950), Dartmouth Conference (1956)
1970s Early Hopes & Limitations: rule-based systems; first AI Winter
1980s Expert Systems Era: knowledge engineering; 1990s AI Rebounds: Deep Blue beats Kasparov (1997)
2000s ML Matures: SVMs, decision trees; deep learning coined (2006)
2010s Deep Learning Revolution: AlexNet (2012), GANs (2014), AlphaGo (2016)
2020s Foundation & Generative AI: GPT-3, ChatGPT, DALL·E, Codex; IndiaAI Mission (2024)
